subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Severe left-sided flank pain
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 52 years old, and I'm here because I think I have a kidney stone. I've been in a lot of pain on my left side for about three days, and it's been getting worse. I haven't passed it yet, and I'm really struggling with the pain. Doctor: Have you experienced any hematuria, nausea, vomiting, or fever associated with the pain? Patient: I did notice some blood in my urine this morning, and I've been feeling pretty nauseous. I haven't had a fever, but I've had some chills. It's been really hard to eat or even get comfortable because of the pain. Doctor: Have you experienced any prior episodes of kidney stones or similar symptoms in the past? Patient: Yes, I've had kidney stones before—this might be my third time. I haven't had one in a while, but I remember the pain being similar each time, and it usually takes about three to four days to pass. Doctor: Have you experienced any fever during this current episode, and if so, what was the highest temperature recorded? Additionally, have you had any prior surgical interventions for kidney stones or related complications? Patient: I haven't had a fever, but I did have some chills. I don't remember having any surgery for kidney stones before. Doctor: Could you describe the location of the pain, whether it radiates to any other areas, and if you have any other symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, or blood in your urine? Patient: The pain started on my left back and has been traveling lower, but it's still mostly on the left side. I haven't passed the stone yet, and I've had some blood in my urine this morning. I also feel really nauseous and can't eat because of the pain. It's been constant and really intense. Doctor: Have you had any recent imaging studies
